quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Computer systems engineers and architects design and develop solutions to complex applications problems, system administration issues or network concerns, and perform systems management and integration.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Computer Systems Engineers/Architects) include Solutions Architect, Systems Architect, IT Architect and Infrastructure Engineer.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Three (medium preparation needed): most occupations in this zone require training in vocational schools, related on-the-job experience, or an associate's degree.

sections.heading: What a solutions architect does
paragraphs: Computer systems engineers and architects design and develop solutions to complex applications problems, system administration issues or network concerns, and perform systems management and integration.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Computer Systems Engineers/Architects. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Talk to staff or clients to understand what a system must do.
Investigate whether system components suit their purpose and recommend which to use.
Direct the analysis, development and operation of complete computer systems.
Monitor system operation to detect potential problems.

sections.heading: How people get into this job
paragraphs: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Three (medium preparation needed): most occupations in this zone require training in vocational schools, related on-the-job experience, or an associate's degree.
O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Common routes into this job on the Career Tree map: Senior Software Engineer; Technical Lead.
Less common routes on the map: Systems Administrator; Data Engineer; Security Engineer.
